qAndA.question: What visual technique is used in Scene 2 to emphasize the seriousness of Psaki's comments about working with President Biden?

qAndA.answer: It highlights the constant scrutiny faced by presidents and the need to develop resilience in the face of criticism.

qAndA.answer: She believes it demonstrates transparency and allows the public to witness the back-and-forth of the political process.
qAndA.question: Why does Psaki emphasize the importance of disagreeing in public?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So you've been at the podium before, not this specific one.
Yes. How did it feel?
You know, even though I had done a similar job at the State Department,
you think, you know, you have the weight of, I want to represent the president,
I want to, I want to meet this moment.
You know, people are watching, I want my mom to be proud, all the things.
But once, once I got out there, it felt great.
And I, I used him as my guide.
That was one of the things we talked about, was how to make sure that I'm aligned
with where he is.
And you know, from having worked for President before, it helps just to listen to them.
I just remember hearing from my boss one morning after he'd read the newspaper,
he said,
MacKinnon, I can get people to say that about me for free.
Yeah.
Well, I am, there will be days where I do not say things in the way that he wants me to.
So I'm prepared for that too.
So, how do you intend to do things differently than the previous administration?
Well, they're not my model.
I think first and foremost, it felt important to me personally to convey yesterday that we
would disagree at times in the briefing room.
And I think it was important for the public to hear that, because that's part of the healthy
back and forth, and that's part of democracy.
So the President Biden is coming with a pledge to bipartisanship, kind of his DNA.
Yeah.
You face a ton of challenges, you got big stuff to do, but how are you going to square the
things you need to do with the partisanship that's most certainly going to come with
an impeachment process?
Well, you know, first we have to kind of keep our blinders on and focus on what we feel
the American public elected him to do, which is to address COVID, address COVID, address
COVID, and get it under control.
Is there a point where you have to put bipartisanship aside to get solutions passed?
You just kind of have to say, we got to rip and go.
Maybe we'll see.
We're not going to wait for a coup d'état if it's delaying getting relief to the public,
but we're going to try for bipartisan package and bipartisan approach first.
And, you know, that requires lots of talks and engagement conversations, but it's our
first goal.
We'll see if it takes.
